page: Amazon Web Services c6gd.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by a 16-core AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 ARMv8 processor. Operating at 2.5 GHz, the CPU features 16 dedicated physical cores with one thread per core, supported by 32.0 GB of system memory, which equates to 2.0 GB per core. The instance is built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and includes 950 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage. Network performance is characterized by a baseline bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates average multi-core and memory performance, alongside weaker single-core capabilities. The instance achieved a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 24,294.54 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 8,497.0, both falling in the middle 50% tier. Memory bandwidth is strong for cached small blocks at 946.78 GB/sec, but drops to 150.22 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Single-core performance is a notable tradeoff, with Geekbench single-core scoring 934.0 and single-threaded bzip3 decompression scoring 7.07 GB/sec, both placing in the bottom 10% of tested servers. Cryptographic and text processing tasks also show weaker performance, with a Passmark encryption score of 2,172.25.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c6gd.4xlarge offers a high density of dedicated physical ARM cores and integrated high-speed local NVMe storage, making it a viable option for workloads that benefit from local scratch space without the added cost of external block storage. It is well-suited for multi-threaded applications, software compilation, static web serving, and database operations, as evidenced by its 19.13 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and 19.25 GB/sec static web serving throughput. However, it is less suitable for single-threaded tasks or heavy cryptographic workloads due to architectural performance limitations.
description: Amazon Web Services c6gd.4xlarge is an ARM64 compute-optimized instance featuring 16 dedicated physical cores powered by an AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processor running at 2.5 GHz. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of RAM, 950 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps. Benchmarks show average multi-core performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 24,294.54, and strong cached memory bandwidth of 946.78 GB/sec. However, single-core performance is a key tradeoff, with Geekbench single-core scores falling in the bottom 10%. The inclusion of local NVMe storage provides qualitative cost efficiency for resource-dense, multi-threaded workloads. This instance is best suited for software compilation, static web serving, and database operations like Redis, while being less optimal for single-threaded or cryptographic tasks.
